{"name":"main","commit":{"sha":"010f6a57610214fa41651861e00319f88a2f49a4","node_id":"C_kwDOTNISa9oAKDAxMGY2YTU3NjEwMjE0ZmE0MTY1MTg2MWUwMDMxOWY4OGEyZjQ5YTQ","commit":{"author":{"name":"DTALEX66","email":"151195992+DTALEX66@users.noreply.github.com","date":"2026-09-29T00:04:59Z"},"committer":{"name":"GitHub","email":"noreply@github.com","date":"2026-09-29T00:04:59Z"},"message":"docs(audit): correct the bundle-list plan's wrong premise and hand over the round (#206)

Two things, both about not letting a plausible-but-wrong claim sit in the repo
unmarked.

1. NEXT-ROUND-PLAN-BUNDLES-LIST.md asserted "a delivery is an asset with
   asset_kind='design-bundle'". PR #205 proved that value is not in the asset CHECK
   constraint at all, so a query on it matches nothing forever. The doc is corrected
   in place: a banner states what was executed, what was wrong, and the real predicate
   (asset_kind='other' AND asset_id LIKE 'bundle-%'). The wrong original text is KEPT
   and marked, not silently rewritten, so the specific error stays legible.

   It also pins a distinction the old snippet got wrong: kind=r['asset_kind'] would
   emit 'other' in the response, but the response label must be 'design-bundle'.
   Column value and API semantics are not the same thing; putting 'design-bundle' back
   in the WHERE clause is the bug, putting it in the response is correct.

   Section 3.2 (the HTTP route) is marked NOT IMPLEMENTED, because it isn't. The
   Bundles class has no route: the service and the UI cannot reach it, only its tests
   can. Nothing here claims otherwise.

2. New docs/handoffs/DESIGN-LAB-BUNDLES-LIST-QUERY-ROUND-2026-09-28.md records the
   round: summary, evidence level (E2, explicitly not E3+), what was left undone, the
   concrete blockers (13 owner decisions, Adobe hardware for E3/E4, host_live 1/28 and
   delivery 0/28), and the dual-end check (local HEAD == origin/main == cloud main ==
   b86c6da, clean, 0 open PRs, 0 stashes, 1 worktree).

   It also records the discipline failure this round earned: git commit -m with a
   message containing a double quote terminated the PowerShell string and the rest of
   the message went to git as pathspecs. The fix, now used, is a written message file
   plus git commit -F. And: gh pr checks --watch exits 1 on ANY failing check including
   advisory ones, so the required-check list must be read from branch protection rather
   than inferred from that exit code.
